description:
Goal

A closure-call result uses the selected executable return contract whenever settled callable demand proves one grounded, non-first-class target. Opaque, escaping, and ambiguous callable invocations retain the public ValueRef contract. Interpreter, JIT, and AOT therefore consume the same producer-owned return shape without boxing and later reconstructing exact captures.

Signal

On integration HEAD 2de30c10c, curried_add passes interp but run/build fail because apply/2 invokes an exact first closure whose target returns the inner closure as two capture lanes, while TransportOrigin unconditionally labels every ClosureCall result PublicCallableReturn. Main resumes that result as one ValueRef and passes it to a specialized apply/2 input that correctly declares the two captures plus one surface argument. Native reports 2 emitted arguments versus 3 declared. Direct two-capture closure returns, non-curried captured closures, and ordinary direct calls pass; the failure requires an exact closure-call result crossing the unconditional public-return classification.

Strategy

Preserve the lowered closure-call producer as ClosureCallReturn { callsite, callee ValueId }. At transport evaluation, refine from the callee values settled RuntimeDemand: a non-first-class singleton target aliases that exact ExecutableReturn product for both shape and callable-owner flow; every other demand remains a public callable return. The transport product records durable RuntimeDemand and target-return dependencies, so later caller-demand replacement invalidates and re-settles provisional public layouts. Do not change IncomingInputSlot, BackendCallArg, native encoding, or wrapper lookup; do not add adapters, padding, identity decoding, registries, provenance, sealing, passes, or fallbacks.

Plan

1. Pin exact closure-call returns to equality with their grounded target ExecutableReturn, including carrier and capture lanes.
2. Pin opaque, exact-but-first-class, and ambiguous multi-target closure-call returns to ValueRef.
3. Pin repeated curried callers and same-session reverse request order: provisional public target returns must refine after root caller demand, with dependent product generation changing.
4. Verify curried_add through interp, run, build, and the built artifact; keep captured, zero-capture, ordinary, and opaque callable controls green.
5. Run library tests, formatting, strict clippy, and inspect the branch-root diff for obsolete concepts and documentation impact.

Acceptance

curried_add matches across interp, JIT, AOT, and the built artifact. Structural tests prove grounded closure-call result shape and callable-owner facts alias the same producer ExecutableReturn; public controls remain ValueRef; replacement and request order converge without schedule-dependent selection. The unconditional PublicCallableReturn semantic-origin concept is removed. No downstream compensation or duplicate callable authority is added.
title: Ground exact closure-call return transport
